name: Chaetopappa

project_scope.source_pool: Live Master Plant Pool; all three already canonical; range statuses unchanged

look_here_first: Check mature stem leaves first: densely overlapping narrow leathery grooved leaves point to C. ericoides. If leaves are flat and uncrowded, expose the base: a taprooted annual is C. bellidifolia; a rhizomatous perennial with broad proximal leaves is C. effusa. Confirm with mature cypsela pappus, not ray color.

shared_traits: Small annual or perennial composites with alternate simple leaves and solitary terminal radiate heads.
Head has ray and disk florets and an involucre of several phyllary series; ripe cypsela/pappus provides critical characters.
All three may have pale rays and yellow disks; flower color and small size are shared, not separating.
priority: Leaf overlap, texture and adaxial grooves
Mature pappus: bristles versus minute ring
Proximal cauline leaf width and base
study_strategy.warning: Detached flowering heads and immature fruits rarely establish a safe species ID. C. bellidifolia and C. effusa BOTH have tiny ringlike pappi.

comparison_cards.look_here_first: Compare whole plant, involucre/phyllaries, and mature fruit rather than pale ray color.

overlap_and_cautions: White/pink rays, yellow disk and small heads overlap.
A broken root does not prove annuality; seek an intact base.
C. parryi resembles rhizomatous effusa but has 2–5 mm proximal leaves and a larger 0.3–0.8 mm hyaline pappus crown.
C. hersheyi resembles leafy ericoides but has a two-series pappus with about five long inner bristles and outer scales.
Small-rayed Erigeron spp. are plausible look-alikes; inspect involucre and mature fruit with an appropriate key, not color.

local_lookalike_routing.check: Whole head, phyllaries, ripe pappus and plant base; no universal visual shortcut.
Proximal leaf width 2–5 mm; pappus crown 0.3–0.8 mm.
Two-series pappus: outer scales and ~5 inner bristles.

anatomy_lessons.title: Leaf overlap and upper-surface grooves
anatomy_lessons.plain_language: Compare same-length leafy stems; C. ericoides has crowded leathery leaves with raised center vein and two upper-face grooves.
anatomy_lessons.measurement: C. ericoides leaves often 2–10 mm long; include mm ruler.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: Matched stem and upper-leaf surface macro for all three.
anatomy_lessons.caution: Leaf crowding varies with drought; uninspected image does not verify grooves.

anatomy_lessons.title: Taproot versus rhizomatous crown
anatomy_lessons.plain_language: Follow intact plant bases. C. bellidifolia is a taprooted annual; C. effusa is rhizomatous; C. ericoides has a woody/rhizomatous base.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: Matched excavated crown and rhizome images.

anatomy_lessons.title: Proximal cauline leaf base
anatomy_lessons.plain_language: Measure lower stem leaves and their bases. C. effusa often has broader oblong leaves with truncate to subcordate bases.
anatomy_lessons.measurement: C. effusa proximal blade width 6–12 mm; C. ericoides leaf length often 2–10 mm.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: Matched lower-stem leaf with millimeter ruler.
anatomy_lessons.caution: Do not compare leaf width against leaf length as if same character.

anatomy_lessons.title: Mature cypsela and pappus
anatomy_lessons.plain_language: Dissect ripe dry fruit. C. ericoides has many white barbellate bristles; C. bellidifolia and C. effusa have minute ringlike pappi.
anatomy_lessons.measurement: C. ericoides usually 24–26 bristles (20–30); C. effusa crown <0.1 mm.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: Matched mature-fruit microscope views with scale.
anatomy_lessons.caution: Minute rings overlap; immature fruit is unreliable.
